speaker: Doctor

The initial CBC and blood culture results are normal, which makes a severe bacterial infection like sepsis less likely. Given the generalized rash in a newborn, have you noticed any blisters, petechiae, or if the skin feels warm or tender to the touch?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood tests and direct Coombs test are normal, which helps rule out severe bacterial sepsis and common immune-mediated causes like hemolytic disease of the newborn. To further investigate the nature of this rash, does the baby have any other symptoms like jaundice, poor weight gain, or do you recall any exposure to a specific illness around the time of birth?

REQUEST TEST: Maternal_Serology (HIV, Syphilis, Rubella, CMV, HSV)
REQUEST IMAGES: Rash_Clinical_Closer_Inspection

speaker: Doctor
text:
The maternal serology is normal, effectively ruling out congenital infections like CMV, Syphilis, or Rubella. Since the CBC and culture were also normal, do you know if the mother has a history of varicella (chickenpox) during pregnancy or if the baby was born in a cluster of similar illnesses?

REQUEST TEST: HSV PCR (Swab from rash)
REQUEST TEST: Varicella_Zoster_Virus_IgG (Maternal)

speaker: Doctor
text:
I have received the normal results for the HSV PCR and Maternal Varicella Zoster Virus IgG, which makes congenital herpes and maternal chickenpox transmission unlikely. Before we conclude, has the mother experienced any vesicular rash (blisters) in her mouth, genitals, or elsewhere recently?

speaker: Doctor
text:
